delta.text: Which part of the simulator matches the transition function δ?

tape.why: The tape holds the symbols. δ says what the machine does with them.

rule-table.why: Each row is one rule of δ: a state and a symbol, then what to write, where to move and the next state.

start-state.why: The start state is q₀, another part of the 7-tuple.

blank.text: In Sipser’s definition, which alphabet holds the blank?

sigma.why: An input never contains the blank, so the blank is not in Σ.

neither.why: The tape holds blanks, so the blank is a tape symbol.

gamma.text: Γ, the tape alphabet, but not Σ
gamma.why: The tape holds blanks, but an input never contains one.

stay.text: Sipser’s δ moves the head left or right. What about the simulator’s move S?

same-work.text: S leaves the head in place. A move right and then a move left can do the same work.
same-work.why: So S makes some machines shorter, but it does not let them do more.

more-power.text: S lets a machine solve problems that Sipser’s machines cannot solve.
more-power.why: Any rule with S can be replaced by a move right and a move left, with one extra state.

two-cells.text: S moves the head two cells to the right.
two-cells.why: S means “stay”: the head does not move.

no-rule.text: In this simulator, what happens when no rule fits the state and the symbol?

waits.text: The machine stays in its state and waits.
waits.why: Nothing could change, so the simulator stops the run.

error.text: The simulator shows an error and does not start.
error.why: That happens when two rules have the same state and symbol. A missing rule only matters during the run.

rejects.text: The machine stops, and the result line says “Rejected”.
rejects.why: Sipser’s δ has a rule for every case, so this only happens in the simulator.

accept-states.text: In Sipser’s definition, how many accept states does a machine have?

any.why: That is how the simulator’s Accept states list works. Sipser’s definition has one: q_accept.

exactly-one.why: The 7-tuple names one accept state, q_accept, and one reject state, q_reject.

none.text: None: the machine accepts when it stops
none.why: The machine accepts only when it enters q_accept.
